violation_type.title: Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials (26 TAC §746.3407(13))
violation_type.short_title: Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials
violation_type.typical_finding: Based on the gatherings during the investigation, it was determined concrete evidence exists to support that the school have not followed the instructions on the sanitizing solution.

finding_variants.text: Based on the gatherings during the investigation, it was determined concrete evidence exists to support that the school have not followed the instructions on the sanitizing solution.
Bleach water and hand sanitizer were within reach of children. It was on the changing table. This was corrected during the inspection when the items were removed.
There were cleaning supplies accessible to children on the changing table. Note:corrected at inspection.

In one classroom, inspector observed three cans of electronic cleaner (dust and lint remover) stored in a cabinet that was accessible to children. NOTE: This was corrected at the time of inspection when caregiver removed and placed the items out of reach of children.
Disenfectant spray was accessible to children waiting in line for the bathroom. This was corrected at inspection when spray can was removed.

In one classroom one spray bottle, containing a mixture of bleach and water, was observed in an unsecured cabinet accessible to children.     In one classroom, one spray bottle, containing a mixture of bleach and water, was observed on a desk and accessible to children.     **NOTE:  This was corrected at time of inspection when caregiver(s) placed the spray bottles out of reach of children.

occurrences.finding: Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: Manufacture instructions for cleaning supplies were not being followed. A cleaner indicating for non-porous hard surfaces was observed to be used on a diaper changing table.     NOTE: Cleaner was also not properly diluted caregiver stated a few drops or finger measurement was added to a full spray bottle of water.

Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: During inspection, bleach and Lysol were found in an unlocked cupboard under the sink in on of the classrooms. This was corrected at inspection when a care giver moved the materials into a locked closet.

occurrences.finding: Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: At time of inspection, a preschool class was observed with gardening fertilizers  in a cabinet at childs reach.     Corrected at inspection.
Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: A bottle of Lysol disinfectant spray was seen sitting on a cabinet within children's reach inside the classroom.

Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: A storage closet containing cleaning supplies  was unlocked. The closet is located in a children's bathroom stall and is accessible to children when not locked. This was corrected at inspection when the lock was realigned and the door was secured.

Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: Two classrooms had shaving cream accessible to children. The children use the shaving cream for sensory play. The shaving cream manufacturer instructions state that it must be kept out of reach of children. This was corrected when the director removed the shaving cream from the classrooms.

Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: During the inspection there were hazardous materials stored in an unlocked cabinet, within the reach of children, located in the preschool restroom. This was corrected during the inspection when the cabinet was safeguarded by staff.

occurrences.finding: Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: Clorox wipes, bleach sanitizing solution, and hand sanitizer was observed stored on the diaper changing tables in infant and toddler room accessible to children during the inspection. This was corrected during the inspection when caregivers were observed removing the hazardous materials and storing them out of the reach of children.
Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: An aerosol spray can of Goo Off Graffiti was used in a classroom causing a strong chemical odor in a room where children are present.

Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: Several closets have chemicals and tools that cannot be accessible to children. Ensure these doors are locked or have other equipment in place to where they cannot be opened.

Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: This standard was evaluated during the investigation and was found to be deficient. A caregiver did not use a spray bottle filled with soap and water as recommended by the manufacturer when the caregiver sprayed the substance on a table as infants were sitting around and facing the table.

Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: One classroom had a pair of adult scissors, bug spray, tape dispenser, and a bottle of children's Ibuprofen stored in an unsecured cabinet accessible to children.     This was corrected at inspection.

Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: In the toddler classroom, a bottle of Clorox bleach and a bottle of "Scrubbing Bubbles" (bathroom cleaner) was stored in the children's bathroom, in an unsecured cabinet under the sink making it accessible to children.     NOTE: CORRECTED AT TIME OF INSPECTION
occurrences.facility_name: A+ Kidz Care Learning Center 3, LLC

occurrences.finding: Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: This standard was reviewed in relation to the reported allegations and found to be deficient. According to manufacturers instructions 100% bleach is required to be diluted with water before use. The caregiver did not complete this before bringing the bleach in the classroom to be used to clean up an accident.

Using, Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials: A open bag of garden soil was observed sitting on a low table accessible to children. This was corrected during inspection when the caregiver was observed removing the bag of soil from the classroom and making it inaccessible to children by placing it in a storage area.
